label: lem:trace-back-bounds
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:trace-back-bounds}
  Suppose that a trace-back path $P$ with $n$ links 
has time projection $d<T_{\bullet}^{*}/4$.
Then the following holds.
\begin{cjenum}
 \item \label{i:trace-back-bounds.colonies} $P$ passes through at most 3
   colonies, for a total space projection of $<2.1{Q} {B} $.
 \item\label{i:trace-back-bounds.time} $d\ge (n-\Delta-1){T_{\bullet}}/2$. 
If the path has no parental links then the factor $1/2$ can be omitted.
 \item \label{i:trace-back-bounds.age} The age progress of $P$ is at most
   $n/{p}_{1}+\Delta+2$. 
\end{cjenum}
head: environment

label: def:gap
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:gap}
Consider an open interval $G=(l,r)$ 
at some time $t$, where $0 < r - l$ is divisible by ${B} $.
                  
                                                                                 
                                                                                
                               
We say that $G$ is a \emph{right gap}\index{gap}
with \emph{size} $|G|=r-l-{B} $ if 
every traceable cell in $G$ can be space-consistent with $r$ only if it is a
germ cell. 
The \index{gap!right-age}\emph{right age} of the gap $G$ is
is the upper bound of the age of these germ cells (it is 0 if the gap contains
no germ cells).
If $G$ is contained in the colony of $r$ then it is called an \emph{interior gap}.
                                                                               
      
A \emph{right bad gap}\index{gap!bad} is a gap of right-age
\begin{align*}
  \lambda\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}(\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}/2+1) 
                     
\end{align*}
containing an interior gap of size~$\ge\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{gap-lb}}}}{B}$. 
If the gap itself is not interior then its right edge is required to be
an exposed right outer cell.
Left gaps are defined similarly.
head: environment
name: Gaps

title: Definition
body_md:
Suppose that in a time interval $[v_{0},v_{1}]$, the gap
$G(t)=(l(t),r(t))$ is defined for all $t$, in such a way that all cells
$r(t)$ are space-consistent with each other, and $G(t_{1})\cap
G(t_{2})\ne\emptyset$ for all $t_{1}$, $t_{2}$ with $|t_{2}-t_{1}|\le 3T^{\bullet}$.
Then $G(t)$ is called a (right) \emph{gap path}, and the \emph{right age} of
the gap path is the maximum of the right ages of the gaps in it.
head: environment
name: Gap path

title: Lemma
body_md:
If a path space-consistent with $r(t)$ has the same
time projection $[v_{0},v_{1}]$ as the right gap path $G(t)$ and has no
germ cells younger than the right age of the gap path then it cannot cross
$G(t)$.
head: environment

label: lem:rn-gap
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:rn-gap}
Recall the definition of $\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{gap-lb}}}}$ in~\eqref{eq:gap-lb}.
Let $P_{1}=(x_{0},v_{0}),\dots,(x_{n},v_{n})$ be a trace-back path
(listed forwards),
let $L,k$ be positive integers with
 \begin{align*}
       L &< {Q} ^{2},
\\   k &< {U}  - 3 L{p}_{2}\lambda.
 \end{align*}
  Assume the following:
 \begin{cjenum}

  \item $y_{0}<x_{0}$ are in the same domain at time $v_{0}$.

  \item The interval $\left[y_{0}-2.1{B} ,x_{0}+3.1{B} \right)$ 
has been noise-free during $(v_{0}-T^{\bullet},v_{0}]$.

  \item\label{i:rn-gap.gap-bds} $y_{0}$ is an exposed left edge at time $v_{0}$ (see 
Section~\ref{sec:edges}), and 
has been the right end of a  bad gap of right-age $k$
during $(v_{0}-T^{\bullet},v_{0}]$.
Its age is not within $\Delta$ steps of any of the age values listed in
Lemma~\ref{lem:exposing} (Exposing),  with \( \Delta \) defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}.

  \item\label{i:rn-gap.in-col}
If $y_{0}$ is a left outer cell then $P_{1}$ is in the same colony.
In this case, let $Z$ be the starting cell of the originating colony.
Otherwise, $Z=\infty$.

  \item\label{i:rn-gap.time-proj-bd}
  $v_{n}-v_{0}\le L\tau_{2}$.

  \end{cjenum}

  Then during $(v_{0},v_{n}]$, a right gap path $G(t)=(l(t),r(t))$ can be
defined, with $r(v_{0})=y_{0}$,
 \begin{align}\label{eq:gap-path.fast}
     r(v_{n}) &\ge  Z\land {\left( y_{0} + 
       {B} {\bigl(\mskip 1mu\frac{|v_{n}-v_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}|^{+}}{3\tau_{2}}-2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}-11\mskip 1mu\bigr)}\right)},
 \end{align}
\( \nonumber |G(t)| >0 \), with right-age $< k + 3 L\lambda{p}_{2}$.
head: environment
name: Running Gap

label: crl:rn-gap
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{crl:rn-gap}
  Assume the conditions of the Running Gap Lemma, further that
$(x_{n},v_{n})$ is not a germ cell younger than $k + 6L\lambda{p}_{2}$.
Then $v_{n}-v_{0} < \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{destr-t}}}}{Q}$.
head: environment
name: Running Gap

title: Proof
body_md:
et $r(v_{0})=y_{0}$, and let $l(v_{0})$ be the leftmost cell such that
the gap $(l(v_{0}),r(v_{0}))$ has right-age $\le k$.
   \begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.inward}
Let $t_{1}>v_{0}$.
Assume that for all $t\le t_{1}$, a gap path $G(t)$ is defined with the
desired properties and in such a way that $(r(t_{1}),t_{1})$ is not a germ
cell younger than $k+6L{p}_{2}\lambda$, and is traceable.
Then $r(t_{1})$ is an exposed edge, space-consistent with $r(v_{0})$.
    \end{step+}
  \begin{pproof}
    \begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.inward.path}
Let us build a path.      
    \end{step+}
    \begin{prooof}
We start by building a backward trace-back path of length $m$
 \[
  P_{2}=((z_{0},w_{0})=(r(t_{1}),t_{1}),\dots,(z_{m},w_{m}))
 \]
ending at time $v_{0}$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:trace-back-bounds} and the bound~\ref{i:rn-gap.time-proj-bd}
gives
 \[
  m \le \Delta+1+2(v_{n}-v_{0})/{T_{\bullet}} \le \Delta+1+2L\tau_{2}/{T_{\bullet}} 
  <  3L\lambda{p}_{2}.           
 \]
The path does not end in a birth; indeed, otherwise $(r(t_{1}),t_{1})$ would be a germ
cell younger than $3L{p}_{1}\lambda$ contrary to the assumption.
It does not enter the gap; otherwise $(r(t_{1}),t_{1})$ would be a 
germ cell younger than $k+3L\lambda{p}_{2}+3L\lambda{p}_{2}$, which was excluded.
Therefore defining $x=P_{2}(v_{0})$ gives $x\ge y_{0}$.
Without loss of generality, we can suppose $x\le x_{0}$.
Otherwise, Lemma~\ref{lem:crossing} (Crossing) implies that path $P_{2}$
crosses $P_{1}$ and we can switch from $P_{2}$ to $P_{1}$ at the meeting
point.
Thus, $x$ is on the interval $[y_{0},x_{0}]$, aligned with $x_{0}$.

Combine $P_{2}$ and the horizontal path $H$ from $(x,v_{0})$ to
$(y_{0},v_{0})$ into a single chain of links.
It has at most $3{Q} $ horizontal links on $H$, 
and then at most $\Delta+1+2(v_{n}-v_{0})/{T_{\bullet}}$
links on $P_{2}$, giving fewer than
 \[
   3{Q}  + 2(v_{n}-v_{0})/{T_{\bullet}} + \Delta+1
 \]
 links.
 We have $r(t)\ge {B}(y_{0}-2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}-11)$. 
                                                          
 Indeed, the only way for \( r(t) \) to move left is via an island (can happen at most once)
 that is then connected to the right end of the gap by healing.
    \end{prooof}

    \begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.inward.exposed}
A protected left edge cannot occur on \( H+P_{2} \).      
    \end{step+}
    \begin{pproof}
      Suppose first that $(y_{0},v_{0})$ is a member or right outer cell,
      or a germ cell with \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Addr\/}}}}>0 \).
Then the large bad gap on its left contains, by the definition of bad gaps,
a gap in the same colony or in the originating colony.
The path $P_{2}$ could cross it only by repeated parental links.
But the size of the gap is too large for using rule $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-revive\/}}}}$, since the field $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}}$
limits the number of applications.
Instead, $P_{2}$ (when traveled forward) would first have to walk right via
parental links to
participate in the creation of a colony and then walk back via parental links through the
expansion process from that colony---for which there is not enough time due 
to~\eqref{eq:compute-start}.     

Suppose now that $(y_{0},v_{0})$ is a left outer cell.
By requirement~\ref{i:rn-gap.in-col}, then the path $P_{1}$ stays in the
colony of $y_{0}$, and hence so does the whole gap path.
Since the cell is exposed, its age is already past the expansion stages.
Walking right, the age of cells on the path $H$ (which remains in the same colony
as well) does not decrease
except when it crosses into another work period (this is taken care of by our Definition~\ref{def:age-lag}
of age progress that uses \( {}\mskip-\medmuskip\mkern5mu\mathbin
  {\operator@font amod}\penalty900
  \mkern5mu\mskip-\medmuskip {U} \)).
Indeed, by Definition~\ref{def:time-consistency} (Time consistency), the ages of siblings
must be non-increasing as one is moving away from the center of the originating colony.
It is also non-decreasing on the trace-back part $P_{2}$, except possibly on the 
$\le\Delta$ horizontal links allowed by that Lemma~\ref{lem:skirting} (Skirting).
Therefore the age of $(r(t_{1}),t_{1})$ cannot be smaller by more than
$\Delta$ than that of $(y_{0},v_{0})$.
If the age is not smaller at all then $(r(t_{1}),t_{1})$ is also exposed, since
the number of steps on the path is not sufficient to get into an expansion stage
of the next work period.
If decreasing the age by $\Delta$ makes it protected, then one of
the cases in Lemma~\ref{lem:exposing} (Exposing) must have occurred within the
last $\Delta$ steps before the age of $(y_{0},v_{0})$: but this has been
excluded by the condition~\ref{i:rn-gap.gap-bds} of the lemma we are proving.

Suppose that $(y_{0},v_{0})$ is a germ cell with \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Addr\/}}}}<0 \).
                                                                   
                                                           
                                                                           
                                                                             
        
                                                                          
                                             
Since it is exposed to the left its age is \( \ge\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}} \),                       
and its address is \( >-{Q} \).
In this case, the same argument works as for left outer cells above.
    \end{pproof}
 \end{pproof}                     

A large gap cannot be closed by the healing rule, but it can be narrowed somewhat.
Suppose that for a gap $G=(l,r)$ the cells $r,r+{B} ,\dots,r+k{B} $ are siblings
with $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Decaying\/}}}}(r+i{B} )=1$, $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}}(r+i{B} )=k-i$.
Then we set $r'=r+k{B}$.
If these conditions are not satisfied then set $r'=r$.
We define similarly, $l'=l-k{B}$ for an appropriate $k$.
The values $l',r'$ will be called the \emph{adjusted edges} of the gap,
and we will write $G'=(l',r')$.
the \emph{adjusted size} is $|G'|=r'-l'-{B} $.
 
 \begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.no-dam}   
Assume that the gap $G(t)$
with the desired properties was defined up to time $f_{0}$, with adjusted size
$|G'(f_{0})|\ge 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}} {B} +2$ and right age $\le k$.
Assume also that in the area where we define the
path further, all cells are unaffected even via neighbors during
$(f_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}},f_{1}]$. 

Then the gap path $G(t)$ can be defined further in $(f_{0},f_{1}]$ in
such a way that as long as $r(t)$ did not reach $Z$:
 \begin{align}\label{eq:progress-right}
     (r(f_{1})-r(f_{0}))/{B}             &\ge
     \frac{f_{1}-f_{0}}{3\tau_{2}}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}-1,
\\\label{eq:progress-size}
       (|G(f_{1})|-|G(f_{0})|)/{B}  &\ge \frac{f_{1}-f_{0}}{3\tau_{3}} - 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}} - 2.
 \end{align}
If $r(t)$ reaches $Z$ it never decreases again.
   \end{step+}
  \begin{pproof}
  Define $G(t)$ as follows.   
Suppose that it was defined up to time $t_{1}$, and let $t_{2}$ be the
next time that is a switching time of either $l(t_{1})+{B} $ or $r(t_{1})-{B} $ 
or $r(t)$.  
  We distinguish the following cases.
   \begin{djenum}

    \item  $t_{2}$ is a switch of $l(t_{1})+{B} $.
  If the switch is an animation creating a
sibling of $l(t_{1})$, then $l(t_{2})=l(t_{1})+{B} $.

    \item  $t_{2}$ is a switch of $r(t_{1})-{B} $.
  If the switch is an animation creating a
sibling of $r(t_{1})$, then $r(t_{2})=r(t_{1})-{B} $.

    \item  $t_{2}$ is a switch of $r(t)$.
  If $r(t_{1})$ dies, then $r(t_{2})$ is the closest cell to the right of
$r(t_{1})$ that is not a germ cell younger than $k+2(t_{2}-f_{0})/{T_{\bullet}}+1$.

    \item  In all other cases, we leave $G(t)$ unchanged.

    \end{djenum}

If $r(t)$ reaches $Z$, it will never decrease again.
Indeed, this happens only if left outer cells were exposed to the left.
Without loss of generality, assume that these outer cells were growth cells.
In this case, $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(Z)>\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}$.  
                          
As $Z$ is protected to the left, the 
healing rule does not create a left neighbor of $Z$.
The only way that $r(t)=Z$ could move left is by the growth rule, but it
does not work for $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(Z)>\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}$.

Let us show
 \begin{align}\label{eq:rn-gap.no-dam.progress.spread}
       (r'(f_{1})-r'(f_{0}))/{B} &\ge {\left\lfloor \frac{f_{1}-f_{0}}{3\tau_{2}}\right\rfloor},
 \end{align}
which will prove~\eqref{eq:progress-right}.
Here we assume that $Z$ has not been reached.
Since the conditions of part~\ref{step:rn-gap.inward} are satisfied, 
the cell $y=r(t)$ is an exposed left edge for all $t\in(f_{0},f_{1}]$.
                                                    
                                                                             
Hence the longest it can take to move $r'(t)$ right is to
have the rule $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-revive\/}}}}$ move $r(t)$ left by 
up to $\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}$ cells; then all of them die by decaying.
The $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-revive\/}}}}$ steps and the killing of the healing cells
take time at most $\tau_{0}$ each, for a total
of \( 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}\tau_{0}=\tau_{2} \),
setting the field $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Decaying\/}}}}$ takes time at most $\tau_{2}$, and the
final killing again time $\tau_{0}$.
                                                                         
                                                  
                 
                                                   
               

Now let us show~\eqref{eq:progress-size}.
The inequality
 \begin{align}\label{eq:rn-gap.no-dam.progress.monot}
        (l'(f_{1})-l'(f_{0}))/{B}  &\le {\left\lceil \frac{f_{1}-f_{0}}{{p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}}\right\rceil}
 \end{align}
follows from the fact that $l'(t)$ can only increase when
it is equal to $l(t)$ and increases via the the growth rule.
But the next application of $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Grow\/}}}}$ is away by a waiting
period\index{period!wait} of length $\ge{p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}$.
         

Let us combine~\eqref{eq:rn-gap.no-dam.progress.monot} 
and~\eqref{eq:rn-gap.no-dam.progress.spread}.
\begin{align*}
   (|G'(f_{1})|-|G'(f_{0})|)/{B}  
  &\ge (f_{1}-f_{0}){\left( \frac{1}{3{p}_{2}T^{\bullet}}-\frac{1}{{p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}}\right)} - 2.
    \end{align*}
Now, using the definition of \( {p}_{3} \) in~\eqref{eq:p_{3}},      
    \begin{align*}
\frac{1}{3{p}_{2}T^{\bullet}}-\frac{1}{{p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}}=\frac{{p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}-3 {p}_{2}T^{\bullet}}{3 {p}_{2} {p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}T^{\bullet}}
\ge \frac{{p}_{3}-3 {p}_{2}\lambda}{3 {p}_{2} {p}_{3}T^{\bullet}}
\ge \frac{1}{3{p}_{3}{T_{\bullet}}},
 \end{align*}
hence the estimate~\eqref{eq:progress-size}.
 \end{pproof}                     
 
 \begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.dam}
   Let $\left[a_{0},a_{1}\right)\times(u_{0},u_{1}]$ be an island with
   $u_{0}\in (v_{0},v_{n}]$.
Then the gap path $G(t)$ with the desired properties can be defined
for $t\in (u_{0},u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}]$.
We will have
 \begin{align*}
        r(u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}) &\ge r(u_{0})-(\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}+9){B} ,
\\ |G(u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}})|&\ge |G(u_{0})|-(2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}+19){B} .
 \end{align*}
                                       
  \end{step+}
  \begin{pproof} 
Let us define $l(t)$ for $t\in(u_{0},u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}]$.
If $a_{0}\le l(u_{0})+5.1{B} $,
then we set $l(t)$ to be the first site $x$ aligned with $l(u_{0})$
to the right of $a_{1}$ and $l(u_{0})+{B} $ that is unaffected even via neighbors.
This definition is justified, since growth or healing
do not have time to add any cell further to the right of $l(u_{0})+{B} $.
Now $l(t)\le l(u_{0})+(5.1+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}+3.1){B} <l(u_{0})+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}+9{B} $.
                      
                 
                                                         
                                                      
                                                                                      
                                
                 
If $a_{0} > l(u_{0})+5.1{B} $, let $l(t)=l(u_{0})+{B} $ since, as noted above,
at most one cell can be added to $l(u_{0})$ by growth or healing during
$\left[u_{0},u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}\right)$.
                      
                 
                                                          
                                                       
                                 
                 
The definition of $r(t)$ is done symmetrically similarly (but only as a lower
bound).
                       
                                               
                                                                           
                                                                                   
                                                                         
                                                         
                                                                           
                                                         

Thus, the island may decrease the gap by at most
$\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}+9{B} $ on one side; with another possible decrease of size ${B} $ on the
other side, this gives the size estimate of statement~\ref{step:rn-gap.dam}.
\end{pproof}                 

In the space-time rectangle considered, at most one island
occurs: 
indeed, \( v_{n}-v_{0}\leT_{\bullet}^{*}/2 \) follows from~\ref{i:rn-gap.time-proj-bd}
and~\eqref{eq:compute-start}.
Use the construction of part~\ref{step:rn-gap.no-dam} up to the time \( u_{0} \) of the
start of the island, then construction of part~\ref{step:rn-gap.dam}
from \( u_{0} \) to \( u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}} \) (or \( v_{n} \),
whichever comes first), then possibly again the 
construction of part~\ref{step:rn-gap.no-dam} from \( u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}} \) to \( v_{n} \), we
defined \( G(t) \) for all \( t\in[v_{0},v_{n}] \).

 \begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.age} For all \( t\in[v_{0},v_{n}] \), the gap
\( G(t) \) has right-age \( \le k+2(t-v_{0})/{T_{\bullet}}+1 \).
In particular, according to the assumed bound on \( v_{n}-v_{0} \),
at time \( v_{n} \), it still has age at most
 \begin{align*}
   k+2(v_{n}-v_0)/{T_{\bullet}}+1 \le k+2L\tau_{2}/{T_{\bullet}}+1 < k+3L{p}_{2}\lambda,
 \end{align*}
as stated in the lemma.
 
    \end{step+}
   \begin{pproof} 
Let \( z_{1} \) be a live cell in \( G(t) \) space-consistent with \( r(t) \),
and let us build a sequence \( (z_{1},w_{1}) \), \( (z_{2},w_{2}) \), \( \dots \)
with \( f_{1}=w_{1}\ge w_{2}\ge\dotsm \) as follows.
Without loss of generality, assume that \( w_{1} \) is a switching time
of \( z_{1} \). 
If \( z_{1} \) is live at \( w_{1}- \) then \( z_{2}=z_{1} \) and \( w_{2} \) is the previous
switching time of \( z_{1} \).
Otherwise, either \( (z_{1},w_{1}) \) is a newborn germ cell, in which case the
sequence ends at \( (z_{1},w_{1}) \), or it has a parent \( (x,u) \).

If \( x\in G(u) \) then \( z_{2}=x \), \( w_{2}=u \).
Let us show that there is no other possibility.
Indeed, otherwise, \( z_{1} \) would have been 
created by animation which, by Condition~\ref{cond:anim,kill}
can only be by healing or growth.
Since \( r(t) \) is exposed, growth can only happen from the left.
We end up with one of the cases of the definition of \( G(t) \) above, and thus
with \( z_{1}\not\in G(w_{1}) \), contrary to the assumption.

By the parent construction, \( w_{2}\le w_{1}-{T_{\bullet}} \), and
 \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(z_{1},w_{1})\le\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(z_{2},w_{2})+1 \). 
The value \( w_{i} \) decreases at least \( {T_{\bullet}}/2 \)
in every step, while the age of \( (z_{i},w_{i}) \) can decrease by at most
1.
Since it can only end in a birth or a germ cell in \( G(t) \), this
and~\ref{i:rn-gap.time-proj-bd} proves the age bound. 
\end{pproof}                         

\begin{step+}{step:rn-gap.finish}
Let us lower-bound the growth of \( G(t) \) for \( t\in[v_{0},v_{n}] \).  
\end{step+}
\begin{prooof}
Since we applied the estimate of part~\ref{step:rn-gap.no-dam} twice and the estimate
of part~\ref{step:rn-gap.dam} once, we get
 \begin{align*}
   (r(v_{n})-r(v_{0}))/{B}  &\ge \frac{|v_{n}-v_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}|^{+}}{3\tau_{2}}-2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}-11,
 \end{align*}
 and
\begin{align*}
    (|G(v_{n})|&-|G(v_{0})|)/{B}
\\                       &\ge \frac{|v_{n}-v_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}}|^{+}}{3\tau_{3}}
     - 4\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}} -2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}-21.
 \end{align*}
 Hence using~\eqref{eq:gap-lb}, \( |G(t)| \) never decreases below
 \( |G(v_{0})|-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{gap-lb}}}}{B} >0 \).
  \end{prooof}
head: environment
name: L

label: lem:healing-cause
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:healing-cause}
  Let \( c_{0}=(x_{0},t_{0}) \) be a cell with \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}}(c_{0})>0 \),
 \begin{alignat*}{3}
      D &= x_{0}+\left[-(\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}+0.1){B} ,(\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}+1.1) {B} \right),
\\   I  &= (t_{0}-2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}T^{\bullet},t_{0}].
 \end{alignat*}
Assume that \( D\times I \) is damage-free.
Then there is a backward path with at most \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}-1 \) horizontal links,
at most 1 parental link, and at most \( 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}} \) links altogether,
connecting \( c_{0} \) to an exposed cell.

A similar statement holds if \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Frozen\/}}}}(c_{0})\ne 0 \), except that here the
length of the path is bounded by \( 2\Delta \), with \( \Delta \)
defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}.

label: lem:colony-trace-back
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:colony-trace-back}
Consider a time interval $(t_{0},t_{1}]$.
Suppose the following, with \( I=z_{0}+\left[-1.1{Q}{B} ,2.1{Q}{B} \right) \):
\begin{enumerate}
\item The rectangle \( I\times (t_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},t_{0}] \) is damage-free,
  and \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Damage\/}}}^{*} \) does not intersect \( I\times(t_{0}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},t_{1}] \).
\item At time $t_{1}$, colony $\mathcal{C}$, with starting cell $z_{0}$,
is covered by a maximal domain with member cells in $\mathcal{C}$, and
no exposed edges.

\end{enumerate}
Assume that some trace-back path \( P \)
starts within $0.2{Q} {B} $ of the center at time $t_{1}$,
goes back to time $t_{0}$, and does not
come within \( 2 {Q}  \) steps of a work period boundary time.
Then:
\begin{cjenum}

  \item\label{i:lem.colony-trace-back.path}
Path \( P \) moves at most to a distance $2\lambda\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}{B}$ from where it started.
If there is no damage in \( I\times(t_{0},t_{1}] \) then \( P \) does not move
horizontally at all.

  \item\label{i:lem.colony-trace-back.cover}
The colony $\mathcal{C}$ is covered by a maximal domain without exposed edges
also at time $t_{0}$.

  \item\label{i:lem.colony-trace-back.progress}
    The age progress from $t_{0}$ to $t_{1}$ along path $P$ is at
most $\frac{t_{1}-t_{0}}{{p}_{1}{T_{\bullet}}}+\Delta + 3$,
and at  least $\frac{t_{1}-t_{0}}{4{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}}-6{Q}$.
\end{cjenum}

title: Proof
body_md:
et $P=(c_{1},c_{2},\dots)$ be the trace-back path mentioned in the lemma,
  listed backwards  in time, with $c_{i}=(x_{i},u_{i})$.
In the given time interval, at most one island intersects colony $\mathcal{C}$.
Let \( K \) be the interval of times within \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}} \) of 
this island, then \( |K|\le 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}}T^{\bullet} \).
                                         

\begin{step+}{step:colony-trace-back.progress.protected}
For times outside \( K \), 
the maximal domain containing the cell \( P(t) \) has only protected edges.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
If there was an exposed edge, then Lemma~\ref{lem:bad-gap-infr} 
(Bad Gap Inference), combined with Lemma~\ref{lem:rn-gap} (Running Gap) would
imply that the colony \( \mathcal{C} \) would not be covered by a domain at time \( t_{1} \).
\end{pproof}                                            

  
\begin{step+}{step:cover-trace-back.path}
Claims~\ref{i:lem.colony-trace-back.path} 
and~\ref{i:lem.colony-trace-back.cover} are true.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
The island may cause at most $\Delta$ horizontal links
(with \( \Delta \) defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}), all other links are
vertical or parental.
As shown in part~\ref{step:colony-trace-back.progress.protected}, the
path can have parental links only within distance $\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}}$ in time of the island.
Since they use $\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}}(\cdot)$ with a delay of at least ${p}_{1}$,
parental links are separated from each other by at least ${p}_{1}$ vertical
links.
If follows then, using the definition of \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}} \) and \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}} \)
in~(\ref{eq:split-n}-\ref{eq:split-t}), that the path can move at most
\(    \Delta+|K|/{p}_{1}{T_{\bullet}} \) steps away, where
 \begin{align*}
   |K|/{p}_{1}{T_{\bullet}}=(2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{island-size}}}})\tau_{2}\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}/{p}_{1}{T_{\bullet}} \le 3\lambda\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}/2
\end{align*}
(and will therefore stay in the colony).
Assume now that, contrary to claim~\ref{i:lem.colony-trace-back.path},
there is a first cell $c_{i}$ with a parental
link to $c_{i-1}$, farther than $\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}}$ in time from the island.
Then $x_{i}$ is at distance at most $\lambda\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-span}}}}\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-n}}}}{B}$ from $x_{1}$, and
as by assumption does not come within \( 2 {Q}  \) steps of a work period boundary time,
is an exposed member cell, or growth cell with age $\ge\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{grow-end}}}}$, inside the the
colony. 
Lemma~\ref{lem:bad-gap-infr} (Bad Gap Inference)
implies then a bad gap which would not close until
time $t_{1}$, contrary to the assumptions.
Reference to the same lemma proves also the
statement~\ref{i:lem.colony-trace-back.cover}. 
\end{pproof}                             

\begin{step+}{step:colony-trace-back.progress}
Claim~\ref{i:lem.colony-trace-back.progress} is true.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
  The upper bound follows because according to
  Lemma~\ref{lem:skirting} (Skirting)
  there are at most \( \Delta+1 \) horizontal links in the path, while
  along the vertical part of the path, age increases at most by 1 every \( {p}_{1} \) steps.
 We proceed to the lower bound.

\begin{step+}{step:colony-trace-back.progress.path}
We will build a new path, \( P'=\mathopen( c'_{0},\dots,c'_{m}\mathclose) \) 
with \( c'_{i}=(x'_{i},t'_{i}) \).
\end{step+}
\begin{prooofi}
Start with \( c'_{0}=c_{0} \).
Within the set \( K \) we continue  \( P' \) as a trace-back path;
consider the cases \( t'_{i}\not\in K \).
We have \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Healing\/}}}}(x'_{i})=0 \) and \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Frozen\/}}}}(x'_{i})=0 \)
for times near \( t'_{i} \), since otherwise
Lemma~\ref{lem:healing-cause} (Healing Cause)
would imply the nearby presence of exposed edges.            
In the absence of freezing, the age cannot decrease in time.
If \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(x'_{i}) \) did not increase in time \( t'_{i} \),
then this can only have the following reasons:
\begin{djenum}
  \item\label{i:delay.wait}
 Cell \( x'_{i} \) is in the process of decreasing its \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Wait\/}}}}.\ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{March\/}}}} \) variable
    from \( {p}_{1} \).
  \item\label{i:delay.parent} Cell \( c'_{i} \) has just been born.
  \item\label{i:delay.neighbor}
 There is a neighbor \( y \) at the last observation time \( t' \) of \( x'_{i} \) that does
 not let its age advance, by condition~\eqref{alg:March.sibling}
 of the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{March\/}}}} \) rule~\ref{alg:March}.
 Thus it is either lower in age (call this a \emph{delay link of the first kind})
 or is equal in age but then it is closer to the center of the originating colony (call it a
 \emph{delay link of the second kind}).
\end{djenum}
In cases~\ref{i:delay.wait} and \ref{i:delay.parent}, let \( c'_{i+1} \) be
 found by regular trace-back: thus, the previous switching time of \( x'_{i} \) if
there is one, and the parent, if \( x'_{i} \) has just been born.
In case~\ref{i:delay.neighbor}, let \( c'_{i+1}=(x'_{i},t') \),
\( c_{i+2}=(y,t') \).
\end{prooofi}                                       

We will now lower-bound age decrease and upper-bound age decrease
backwards on path \( P' \).

\begin{step+}{step:colony-trace-back.progress.inK}
Let us upper-bound age increase inside the set \( K \).
\end{step+}
\begin{prooofi}
Inside the time set \( K \), the only horizontal links
on the path \( P' \) come from Lemma~\ref{lem:skirting} (Skirting),
adding at most \( \Delta \) to the total age increase backward.
There is no increase on parental links, and at most one backward increase on each
vertical link (as \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-sync\/}}}} \) may decrease age).
                                                                 
                                         
                                                                        
This is a total increase of at most \( |K|/{T_{\bullet}}+\Delta \).
\end{prooofi}                                      

\begin{step+}{step:colony-trace-back.progress.nonK}
Let us lower-bound age decrease outside the set \( K \).
\end{step+}
\begin{prooofi}
Going to the parent via
alternative~\ref{i:delay.parent} above is always going towards the
originating colony:
since we are in a maximal domain without exposed edges, the only possible kind
of cell creation is growth.
The cells created by growth have age equal to the creator cell.
During a colony work period, there are at most \( 4{Q}  \) growth steps (growing a
channel and then a growth arm to the left, and also to the right), this bounds the
number of parental links.
Let \( n_{1} \) be the number of delay links of the first kind and \( n_{2} \) that of
delay links of the second kind, \( n=n_{1}+n_{2} \).
We have
\(  n_{2}\le 2 {Q}  + n_{1} \), as one can move towards the center
of the originating colony only after being moved away from it.
The total age decrease on these non-vertical links is hence at least
\(  n_{1}\ge n/2 -  {Q}  \).
The total number of non-vertical links is \( m \le 4 {Q}  + n \), so
\begin{align}\label{eq:n1-lb}
  n_{1}\ge (m-4 {Q} )/2 - {Q}  = m/2 - 3 {Q} .
\end{align}
In a vertical segment of the path of time projection \( l \),
age decreases at least by 1 in every \( {p}_{1} \) vertical steps.
So it decreases at least \( 0\lor(\frac{l}{{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}}-1) \).
Let us call a vertical segment \emph{short} if this number is \( <1 \),
that is whose length is \( \le 2{p}_{1}T^{\bullet} \), else \emph{long}.
On a long segment of length \( l \), the decrease is at least
\( \frac{l}{{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}}-1 \ge \frac{l}{2{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}} \).
Let \( L_{1} \) be the union of long vertical segments, and \( L_{2} \) that
of the short ones.
The time decrease on \( L_{1} \) is at least \( \ge |L_{1}|/2{p}_{1}T^{\bullet} \).
The number of non-vertical links is at least \( m\ge |L_{2}|/2{p}_{1}T^{\bullet} -1\),
and by~\eqref{eq:n1-lb} the age decrease on these links is at least
\begin{align*}
   m/2 - 3 {Q}  \ge |L_{2}|/4{p}_{1}T^{\bullet} -3 {Q}  - 1.
 \end{align*}
So the total decrease of at least
\begin{align*}
  |L_{1}|/2{p}_{1}T^{\bullet} + |L_{2}|/4{p}_{1}T^{\bullet} -3 {Q}  - 1
  \ge \frac{t_{1}-t_{0}-|K|}{4{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}}- 3{Q}  - 1.
\end{align*}
\end{prooofi}                                       

\begin{step+}{step:colony-trace-back.progress.sum}
Let us add up all the decreases inside and outside of \( K \).
\end{step+}
\begin{prooofi}
We get
 \begin{align*}
     &\frac{t_{1}-t_{0}-|K|}{4{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}}-3{Q} -1 - |K|/{T_{\bullet}}-\Delta =  \frac{t_{1}-t_{0}-|K|}{4{p}_{1}T^{\bullet}}-V,
\\ V &\le 3{Q}  +|K|/{T_{\bullet}}+\Delta+1 \le 4 {Q} ,
 \end{align*}
where the last step follows from our assumptions about \( {Q}  \).           
At time \( t_{0} \), there is no exposed edge between 
\( P(t_{0}) \) and \( P'(t_{0}) \), since this would imply a bad gap between these cells.
This could not close, and at least one of the paths would need to cross
it in order to meet, which is not possible.           
Therefore these two nodes are connected by a chain of siblings and so
their age differs by at most \( 2{Q}  \).
Since \( P(t_{1})=P'(t_{1}) \), this shows that the age progress along \( P \) differs from that
of \( P' \) by at most \( 2{Q}  \).
\end{prooofi}                                      
\end{pproof}

body_md:
\label{lem:heal}\index{lemma@Lemma!Healing}
Let \( \left[a_{0},a_{1}\right)\times(u_{0},u_{1}] \) be an island. 
Let \( \mathcal{C} \) be a colony with starting cell \( z_{0} \), 
covered at time \( u_{0} \) by a        
domain of member cells, with no doomed cells of age \( >{U} -3{Q}  \).
Then a domain covers \( \mathcal{C} \) at time \( w_{0}=u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{heal-t}}}} \).
head: environment
name: Healing

title: Proof
body_md:
he damage affects directly at most \( \Delta \) neighbor cells of \( \mathcal{C} \)
   (with \( \Delta \) defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}).
At time \( t \), let \( L(t) \) be the set of successors in \( \mathcal{C} \) of 
cells of \( \mathcal{C} \) on the left of the affected part, and \( R(t) \) the successors from
cells to the right.
(These sets are not necessarily disjoint.)
Both \( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) are (possibly empty) domains; indeed,
the only rule that would change the domain property is the killing
of a doomed cell at age 0, but there is not enough time for this. 
                                 
                                            
                                                   
                                                                                
                                                          
                                                                                         
                                                       

                                                               
                                                                             

\begin{step+}{step:heal.purge}
Let \( u_{2}=u_{1}+\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{purge-t}}}} \).
If the sets \( L(u_{2}) \) and \( R(u_{2}) \) are both nonempty
then there is no live cell between them at time \( u_{2} \)
other than possibly germ cells with age \( \le 1 \).
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
The only cells in question are the up to \( \Delta \) cells affected directly by the
damage, others could not have reborn yet after dying.
Consider the up to \( \Delta \) domains between \( L(u_{1}) \) and \( R(u_{1}) \);
they can shrink or merge during the time interval \( (u_{1},u_{2}] \).
According to Lemma~\ref{lem:short-exposed}, each will still have an exposed side,
hence each will be killed by the time \( u_{2} \) by
the purge rule (while having no time yet to grow due to the delay in the
rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \))---unless they are germs so new
that the purging did not have time to finish yet: in this case they have age \( \le 1 \).            
\end{pproof}             

\begin{step+}{step:heal.purge-end}
Any live cell at time \( u_{2} \) whose body intersects \( \mathcal{C} \) and that
does not belong to \( L(u_{2})\cup R(u_{2}) \) cannot be a member cell.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
  Assume by way of contradiction, that there is such a member cell \( x \).
  In this case clearly either \( L(u_{2}) \) or \( R(u_{2}) \) is empty; without
  loss of generality assume that \( L(u_{2}) \) is empty.
Consider a trace-back path from \( x \).
It cannot lead to \( \mathcal{C} \) at time \( u_{0} \), since then according  to  part~\ref{step:heal.purge}
above, \( x \) would belong to either \( L(u_{2}) \) or \( R(u_{2}) \).
Therefore it must lead to a domain outside; given that \( R(u_{2}) \) is nonempty, this must be on the left.
Let \( y \) be the right end of this domain at time \( u_{0} \).
It must be outside \( \mathcal{C} \), so it is to the left of \( x \) whose body, by assumption, intersects \( \mathcal{C} \).
By Lemma~\ref{lem:skirting} (Skirting), the path has at most \( \Delta \) horizontal links,
and one parental link (there is no time for a complete animation delay),
so \( x \) and \( y \) are within distance \( (\Delta+1){B}  \) from each other.
All cells of the short chain from \( (x,u_{2}) \) to \( (y,u_{0}) \) 
have ages within a few steps of each other.
If \( (y,u_{0}) \) is a right colony end then \( x \)
(assumed to be a member cell to the left of \( R(u_{2}) \))
would have been purged away due to its small depth.
If it is not then the right edge of \( (y,u_{0}) \)  is exposed,
since it is either a member cell not at a colony end or a growth cell near the end
of the work period, and so during its shrinking phase.
But then Lemma~\ref{lem:bad-gap-infr} (Bad Gap Inference) 
would imply large gap on the right of \( (y,u_{0}) \), making the path from it
to \( (x,u_{2}) \) impossible.
(Indeed, due to the age of \( (y,u_{0}) \) the
conclusion~\ref{i:bad-gap-infr.exposing} of that lemma is not applicable.)
\end{pproof}                 

                                   
                                                                                        
                                       
             
                
                      
                                                                    
                                                                              
                                                                      
               
                                                                                      
                                                                                                   
                 
                                               
                                                          
                                                                                                 
                              

\begin{step+}{step:heal.size}
If both \( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) survive until time \( u_{2} \), then
the gap between them will have size \( \le \Delta \) during the whole time.
If \( L(t) \) disappears then the 
the gap from \( z_{0} \) to \( R(t) \) has size \( \le 2\Delta \) during the whole time.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
If both \( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) survive, then there were up to \( \Delta \) cells
affected by damage between them.
Only these cells can disappear.
If \( L(t) \) disappears, this is only since its size was \( \le\Delta \) to begin with.
\end{pproof}           

 \begingroup\@ifundefined{if@tlamode}{}{\if@tlamode\tlachars\relax}\endgroup
\begin{step+}{step:heal.no-gap}If both \( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) remain nonempty
then they will become part of a domain.\end{step+}
 \begin{pproof}
As shown above, between times \( u_{2} \) and \( w_{0}  \), the gap between
\( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) does not become larger than \( \Delta \).
Rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-revive\/}}}} \) brings together \( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) 
at some time \( t\le \Delta\tau_{1} \), at  some point \( x\in L(t) \), \( x+{B} \in R(t) \).
The possible germ cells of age \( <2 \) in the gap are not an obstacle: they
are weaker than the cells that are being created, so they will be erased.
It can only happen that \( L(t) \) and \( R(t) \) are not joined if
\( |\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(x)-\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(x+{B} )\mskip-\medmuskip\mkern5mu\mathbin
  {\operator@font amod}\penalty900
  \mkern5mu\mskip-\medmuskip {U} |>1 \).
But as said in the remark at the end of Example~\ref{xpl:heal-sync},
then rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Heal-sync\/}}}} \) will bring the two ages together
in time at most \( 2\Delta\tau_{0} \).           
This creates a single domain by time 
\( u_{2}+\Delta(\tau_{1}+2\tau_{0}) \). 
 \end{pproof}              

 \begingroup\@ifundefined{if@tlamode}{}{\if@tlamode\tlachars\relax}\endgroup
\begin{step+}{step:heal.fill}If \( L(t) \) does not survive then \( z_{0}\in R(w_{0}) \).\end{step+}
  \begin{pproof}
The left endcell of \( R(t) \) will be exposed to the left and therefore the
rule~\ref{alg:End-heal} (\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{End-heal\/}}}} \)) will apply to it.
Part~\ref{step:heal.purge-end} above shows that no member cell's body intersects the
colony \( \mathcal{C} \).
Other possible cells that might intersect are weaker than the member cells that
end-healing creates,
and will therefore be killed off by rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Adapt\/}}}} \) of Algorithm~\ref{alg:Adapt}.
The end healing thus proceeds in time \( 2\Delta\tau_{1} \).
 \end{pproof}

\label{lem:mail-speed}
  Consider a case of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Post-mail\/}}}}(1,\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}},\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{G\/}}}},1,0,0,{Q}) \) when a track \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}} \) is sent to a track \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{G\/}}}} \)
  of a right neighbor colony (not necessarily adjacent).
  Assume that between the sending time \( t_{0} \) and the receiving time,
  the space-time area of concern is damage-free.
  For a cell \( x \) let \( d(x) \) be the distance of \( x \) from the right end of the
  receiving range.
                                                                                                  
                                                                                              
                                                                             
  Let \( x \) be a cell and \( y \) be a cell that is \( m \) steps
  (over neighbors) to the right of \( x \).
  Then at time \( t_{0}+2T^{\bullet}(m+2 d (x)) \) the information from \( x \) has reached \( y \).

label: def:the-err-corr-code
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:the-err-corr-code}
Our error-correcting code will distinguish, similarly to  
Examples~\ref{xmp:err-corr-code} and \ref{xmp:no-stretch}, information symbols
and error-check symbols.
A string $s$ of symbols that can be the argument of a
certain error-correcting decoding \emph{has $d$ errors}\index{error} if,
when applying the decoding and encoding to it, the result differs from $s$
in $d$ symbols.
We will work with a code 
\gloproca.greek@$\alpha$.))) 
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:err-corr-code-alpha}
  \alpha
 \end{equation}
of  Example~\ref{xmp:RS-code} that can
correct errors in $t$ symbols with just $2t$  error-check symbols.
When $\ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{loc\/}}}$ is a location representing a string $s$ then we will use the
notation
 \[
   \alpha^{*}(\ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{loc\/}}})=\alpha^{*}(s)
 \]
 for the value decoded from it.
 We expect having to deal with at most one  damage rectangle.
 It can corrupt a group of \( \Delta \)  
 consecutive cells (where \( \Delta \) was defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}).
The symbols of the code will be chosen in such a way that a code symbol 
stretches over $\Delta$ cells.
A damage rectangle can damage therefore up to 2 symbols, for which 4 error check
symbols suffice.

label: def:packets
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:packets}
  As the payload of a simulated cell is the aggregated payload of the cells
  of its simulated colony, we define the \emph{payload capacity} as
  \begin{align*}
   \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Cap\/}}}'_{k}=|\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}}_{k}|={B}_{k}|\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}}_{1}|.
  \end{align*}
                 
                                                                                                   
                                                                   
                                                                    
                                                                                    
                                                                                                
                                                                             
We partition the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}} \) field
into \( P \) sub-fields of relative width
\( w \) called \emph{field packets} numbered \( 0,1,\dots,P-1 \).
The \( i \)th field packet of the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}} \) field will be denoted \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}}_{i} \).
We also partition each track \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}} \) of whole colony into \( P^{*} \) \emph{track packets}
of \( w^{*}{Q}  \) cells each.
The \( j \)th track packet, with addresses in \( \left[jw^{*}{Q},(j+1)w^{*}{Q}\right) \),
will be denoted as the \emph{location} \( \_\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{F\/}}}}_{j} \),
In particular the \( j \)th track packet of the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}} \) track is location \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j} \)

label: def:PlRedun
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:PlRedun}
The error checks of track packet \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j} \), will be in location
  \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Pl-redun\/}}}}_{j} \) on the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Pl-redun\/}}}} \) track.
Location 
\begin{align}\label{eq:lPayload'}
   \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}'_{j}=\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j}\cup\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Pl-redun\/}}}}_{j}
\end{align}
combines location \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j} \) with its error check symbols for a complete code.

We consider the whole \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}} \) track
of each consecutive \( \Delta \) cells in the packet \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j} \) as an
information symbol; the error check symbols of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j} \) go to
location \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Pl-redun\/}}}}_{j} \).
To avoid that the damage rectangle affect both an information symbol and an error-check symbol
of the same code, we divide the track packet \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}'_{j} \) into left and right halves.
The error checks for the left half of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}_{j} \) go into the right half of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Pl-redun\/}}}}_{j} \),
and those for the right half go into the left half of the same.

If the \( (x,t) \) is not in \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Damage\/}}}^{*} \), then define
 \[
 \eta^{*}(x,t)=\varphi^{*}(x,t)=\ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{Vac\/}}},
 \]
 unless there is a latest time \( t'\in (t-2{Q} T^{\bullet},t] \) that is a switching time
of a cell of \( \mathcal{C}(x) \) such that the rectangle
\begin{align*}
 \left[x-({Q} +1.1){B} ,x+(2{Q} +1.1{B} )\right)\times(t'-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},t']  
\end{align*}
is damage-free, and the colony is covered by a domain of 
cells belonging to the same work period
(the condition on switching just makes sure that a ``latest'' value exists).
In the latter case, let us define the 
strings \( s=\eta(\mathcal{C}(x),t').\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Util\/}}}} \) and \( p_{i}=\eta(\mathcal{C}(x),t').\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{\_Payload\/}}}}'_{i} \).
For the decoded value to be nonvacant, we also require that each of \( s,p_{i} \)
contains at most 4 errors in the sense that \( \alpha_{*}(\alpha^{*}(s)) \) differs
from \( s \) in at most 4 places of up to 2 consecutive symbols) and the same for each \( p_{i} \)
for \( i=0,\dots,P^{*}-1 \).
              
If this is satisfied, then \( \eta^{*}(x,t).\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}}^{c}=\alpha^{*}(s) \) while
\( \eta^{*}(x,t).\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Payload\/}}}} \) is the concatenation of all \( \alpha^{*}(p_{i}) \).
We will say that \( \eta(\mathcal{C}(x),t) \) is \emph{error-free} if each of \( s,p_{i} \) are error-free.

name: Legality

title: Proof
body_md:
et \( I=\left[x,x+{Q}  {B} \right) \).
Our assumption implies that damage is covered by at most one island in 
\( I\times(a-2T^{\bullet *},a+2T^{\bullet *}] \).
             
According to Definition~\ref{def:decoding} (Decoding), there is a latest time \( v_{2} \) 
in \( (\sigma_{2}-2{Q}T^{\bullet},\sigma_{2}] \) that is a switching time
of a cell of colony \( \mathcal{C}(x) \) such that \( I \) is damage-free during
\( (v_{2}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},v_{2}] \), and at time \( v_{2} \) the colony
is covered by a domain of cells belonging to the same work period.
The value \( \eta^{*}(x,\sigma_{2}) \) was decoded from the state of the colony at
time \( v_{2} \).
Let \( y_{1} \) be the cell with address \( {\lfloor {Q} /2\rfloor} \) in colony
\( \mathcal{C}(x) \), then \( (y_{1},v_{2}) \) is traceable, as in
Definition~\ref{def:traceable}.
Build a trace-back path from \( (y_{1},v_{2}) \) 
to the latest time \( v_{1} \) in
\( (\sigma_{1}-2{Q}T^{\bullet},\sigma_{1}] \) at which the colony is again covered with
member cells belonging to the same work period,
moreover \( I \) is damage-free during \( (v_{1}-\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}},v_{1}] \). 
There is such a time, due to the definition of \( \sigma_{1} \).
                                                                                     
Since \( \sigma_{1},\sigma_{2} \) are defined, 
the colony \( \mathcal{C}(x) \) encodes at time \( v_{1} \) with at
most 4 errors a big cell with value different from the one
encoded at time \( v_{2} \).

\begin{step+}{step:legality.free}
If \( I \) is damage-free during \( (v_{1},v_{2}] \) then
claim~\ref{i:legality.legal} holds.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
The computation runs now without faults, and as planned, computes an error-free
value.
Rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Compute\/}}}} \) in Algorithm~\ref{alg:Compute} applies \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Legalize\/}}}} \) to
the information retrieved from the neighbor colonies, so the result
computed from this information will be a legal one.
The switching time \( \sigma_{2} \) occurs just when the last cell of the colony
passes to a new work period. 
The process makes sure that either all cells of the colony are doomed (when the
computed value is vacant), or none them.
If they are doomed then the whole colony dies.
Otherwise, the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Finish\/}}}} \) installs the remaining changes in one step.
In both cases, the state at time \( \sigma_{2} \) will be a legal consequence of
the state at time \( \sigma_{2}- \).
\end{pproof}                     

\begin{step+}{step:legality.non-free}
If \( I \) is not damage-free during \( (v_{1},v_{2}] \) then 
claim~\ref{i:legality.legal} still holds.
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
Let \( t_{1}\in(v_{1},v_{2}] \) be some time at which damage intersects \( I \),
and let \( t_{0} \) be the latest time before \( \min(t_{1}-1.1\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{destr-t}}}}{Q}, v_{1}) \) which is the
switching time of some cell, with the
property that all cells of the colony belong to the same work period.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:cover} (Cover), at time \( t_{0} \), the colony is covered by a
domain of cells.
Lemma~\ref{lem:free-past} implies that the colony encodes an error-free string.

Let us follow the development of the colony forward in time, 
starting from \( t_{0} \).
Healing succeeds, due to the Cover Lemma.
Locally maintained fields will be restored in a short time following the
occurrence of damage, via the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Loc-maintain\/}}}} \) while other fields
changed in at most an interval of \( \Delta \) cells, with \( \Delta \)
defined in~\eqref{eq:numDirAff}.
After this, the work of the colony can be followed as before.

The time of the damage may fall into at most one of the three iterations of
any of the rules with three iterations (\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Refresh-payload\/}}}} \), \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Update-payload\/}}}} \),
\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Legalize\/}}}} \),  \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Compute\/}}}} \)).
The output of this one iteration in \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Vote\/}}}}_{r} \)
will be outvoted by the other two values in the final majority vote.
                                                                                          
                                                 
So the only errors in \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Hold\/}}}} \) can be the ones due
to their short-term damage in the final majority vote; 
these change at most \( \Delta \) cells.
In summary, we can make the same conclusion as
part~\ref{step:legality.free}, except that the encoded string may contain up to
2 errors (in case the island occurs in the last part of computation or later).

There is an exception to this reasoning: in the rules \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Refresh-payload\/}}}} \) and
\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Update-payload\/}}}} \), the copy command is not repeated three times, so
it is protected from the damage only in a limited
way in the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Move-mail\/}}}} \) of Algorithm~\ref{alg:move-mail-2}.
This protection makes sure that wrong information planted by damage 
is copied to at most one segment of size \( \Delta \); however, that one segment
will still be affected, so the damage rectangle can cause 2 errors in the place it occurs and 2
more in the place to which the information is carried.
But the error-correcting code, being able to correct 4 errors, will still deal with this.
\end{pproof}                         

\begin{step+}{step:legality.time-lb}
We have \( T_{\bullet}^{*} \le \sigma_{2} - \sigma_{1} \).
 \end{step+}
 \begin{pproof}
Consider a cell \( y \) of the colony,
for example the one with address \( {\lfloor {Q} /2\rfloor} \), and lead a trace-back path from
time \( \sigma_{2} \) to time \( \sigma_{1} \).
Suppose it has \( n \) links: none of these are parental.
At time \( \sigma_{j}- \) all cells have ages \( \ge {U} -2{Q}  \),          
hence the age progress along the path is at least \( {U} -2{Q}  \).

By Lemma~\ref{lem:trace-back-bounds}, the age progress is 
\( {U} -2{Q} \le n/{p}_{1}+\Delta+2 \), hence 
 \begin{align*}
   n\ge {p}_{1}{U} -{p}_{1}(2{Q} +\Delta+2).
 \end{align*}
By the same lemma, 
 \begin{align*}
\sigma_{2}-\sigma_{1} &\ge n{T_{\bullet}}-(\Delta+1){T_{\bullet}} 
\\ &\ge {T_{\bullet}}{\left( {p}_{1}{U}  -{\left( 2{p}_{1}{Q} +({p}_{1}+1)\Delta+2{p}_{1}+1\right)}\right)}
\\ &=  {T_{\bullet}}{U}' -{T_{\bullet}}{\left( 2{p}_{1}{Q} +({p}_{1}+1)\Delta+2{p}_{1}+1\right)}
   \\ &=  {T_{\bullet}}{U}'{\left( 1-{\left( 2{p}_{1}{Q} +({p}_{1}+1)\Delta+2{p}_{1}+1\right)}/{U}'\right)}
\\ &\ge{T_{\bullet}}{U}' (1-R{Q}/{U}') = {T_{\bullet}}^{*},
 \end{align*}
 where we used~\eqref{eq:U-def}, further
 \( {U}'={U}'_{k} \) was defined in Section~\ref{sec:amp}.
Indeed, sufficiently large \( R \) will satisfy the last inequality.
\end{pproof}                       

\begin{step+}{step:legality.time-ub}
We have \( \sigma_{2} - \sigma_{1}\leT^{\bullet *} \).
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
  Lemma~\ref{lem:colony-trace-back} (Colony Trace-back) lower-bounds
the progress along a trace-back path;
then the proof is finished similarly to part~\ref{step:legality.time-lb} above.
\end{pproof}                        
\begin{step+}{step:legality.rand}
 Let us prove~\ref{i:legality.rand}. 
\end{step+}
\begin{prooof}
  We need to prove essentially \( \operatorname{\mathsf P}\mathopen\{\mskip 1mu\eta^{*}(x,\sigma_{2}).\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Rand\/}}}}=j\mskip 1mu\mathclose\}\le 1/2+eps'+\varepsilon'' \),
  given how \( \varepsilon'_{k} \) is defined in~\eqref{eq:eps-defs}.
  Here \( \varepsilon'' \) bounds the probability that damage occurs in the window \( W_{0}(x,a) \) at all.
  On the other hand, when it does not occur then each cell at each time within the work period
  performs its needed action: in particular, it carries out the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Compute\/}}}} \) of
  Algorithm~\ref{alg:Compute}, and within it, the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Randomize\/}}}} \).
  This rule relies on the randomization action of a well-defined cell at a well-defined age
  of the work period, with the result being \( j \) with probability \( \le 1/2+\varepsilon' \).
  The probability can only be increased by the probability bound that damage does occur in \( W_{0} \).
  It would be now just a tedious exercise to actually express \( g(\alpha(\ensuremath{\mathord{\textit{rand\/}}}),j, W_{0}(x,a),\eta^{*}) \)
  formally as needed by a canonical simulation.
\end{prooof}

label: lem:present-attrib
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:present-attrib}
 \index{lemma@Lemma!Present Attribution}
 Assume that the live cell \( c_{0}=(x_{0},t_{0}) \) in colony \( \mathcal{C}(z_{0}) \)
 is not a germ.                                                               
  Assume also that \( \mathcal{C} \) at time \( t_{0} \) does not intersect the healing
wake of any island.
  Then one of the following cases holds.
 \begin{djenum}

  \item\label{i:present-attrib.center}
  \( c_{0} \) is a member cell, attributed to \( \mathcal{C} \) which is covered by a domain
of member cells at time \( t_{0} \).
If \( {Q}  <\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(c_{0}) <{U} -1-{Q}  \) then every encoded package of this colony
has at most 4 errors.

  \item\label{i:present-attrib.new}
  \( c_{0} \) is a member cell from which a path of time projection at most
  \( {Q} \tau_{2} \) leads back to a growth cell in \( \mathcal{C} \).
  Assume, say, that it is a left growth cell; then it can be attributed to \( \mathcal{C}+{Q} {B}  \).
  At time \( t_{0} \), if \( \mathcal{C}+{Q} {B}  \) does not intersect the healing wake of an
island then \( \left[x_{0},z_{0}+2{Q} {B} \right) \) is covered by a multi-domain.
If \( {Q}  <\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}(c_{0}) <{U} -1-{Q}  \) then still every encoded package of this colony
has at most 4 errors.

  \item\label{i:present-attrib.ext}
    \( c_{0} \) is an outer cell, attributed to its originating colony, say \( \mathcal{C}+ {Q}  {B}  \).
    If \( \mathcal{C}+{Q} {B}  \) does not intersect the healing wake of an
    island then \( \left[x_{0},z_{0}+2{Q} {B} \right) \) is covered at time \( t_{0} \)
    by a domain.

  \item\label{i:present-attrib.vanish}
  \( c_{0} \) is a member cell, and there is in \( \mathcal{C} \) a backward path from
it, with time projection \( \le 2\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{split-t}}}}+({Q} +1)\tau_{2} \),
to a domain of doomed member cells covering \( \mathcal{C} \).

 \end{djenum}
head: environment
name: Present Attribution

title: Proof
body_md:
\begin{step+}{present-attrib.old-member}
Suppose that \( c_{0} \) is a member cell.
  \end{step+}
  \begin{prooof}
    \begin{sloppypar}
      Recall the notation \( K,E_{0} \) from~\eqref{eq:J-K} and
Definition~\ref{def:attrib} (Attribution).
By Lemma~\ref{lem:attrib} (Attribution), \( c_{0} \) can be attributed to the originating
colony \( \mathcal{C} \) which is either the colony of \( c_{0} \) or not.
Let time \( t_{1}\in K\setminus E_{0} \) be a time when \( \mathcal{C} \) was covered by member cells.
Using Lemma~\ref{lem:colony-trace-back} (Colony Trace-back),         
we can go back from \( t_{1} \) to a time \( t_{2} \)
before age \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{compute-start}}}} \) in \( \mathcal{C} \).
Then as in part~\ref {step:legality.non-free} of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:legality}
(Legality), we can follow the development of the colony forwards and see that it
forms a continuous domain together with its extension.
The locations containing encoded information have at most
4 errors---as seen in the same proof.      
    \end{sloppypar}

If the computation results in a nonvacant value for the represented big
cell then, if \( \mathcal{C}=\mathcal{C}(z_{0}) \) then case~\ref{i:present-attrib.center} holds.
The condition \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}>{Q} \) guarantees that all cells of the colony belong to the same
work period.
Otherwise the represented field \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Creating\/}}}}_{j} \) of the colony will be broadcast
into the field \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Growing\/}}}}_{j} \) of its cells, as shown in 
Lemma~\ref{lem:update-loc-maint}.
The homogeneity of this latter field will be maintained by the healing rule and \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Loc-maintain\/}}}} \).
Thus, depending on the value of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Creating\/}}}}_{j} \) of the big cell, growth
will take place and the growth forms a continuous domain with the
originating colony until the age \( {U} \) when growth cells turn into members,
and we have case~\ref{i:present-attrib.new}.
By the property of the growth rule
the colony encodes a latent big cell, so the statement about errors also holds.

Suppose that the computation results in a vacant value.
Then \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Growing\/}}}}_{j} \) will be 0 everywhere but in the healable wake of
the damage.
Growth cannot start accidentally by a temporary wrong value
\( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Growing\/}}}}_{j}=1 \) in an endcell since there is enough time to correct
this value during the long waiting time of \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Grow\/}}}} \).          
Also, all cells become doomed.
After \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}=1 \), any doomed cell dies, and
the whole colony decays within \( {Q} \tau_{2} \) time units.
Before that, the colony is full.
After that, we have case~\ref{i:present-attrib.vanish}.
\end{prooof}                            

  \begin{step+}{present-attrib.outer}
  If \( c_{0} \) is an outer cell then we have case~\ref{i:present-attrib.ext}.
  \end{step+}
  \begin{pproof}
  Lemma~\ref{lem:attrib} (Attribution) attributes \( c_{0} \) to the originating colony which is
  covered by member cells during \( K\setminus E_{0} \).
  If \( c_{0} \) is a channel cell then this colony would not have time until \( t_{0} \)
  even to finish its computation, so it could not be destroyed.
  If \( c_{0} \) is a growth cell then the
  cell represented by this colony could not have become vacant, because
  then \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Creating\/}}}}^{*}_{j} \) would have become 0, broadcast as \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Growing\/}}}}=0 \) and so
  no growth would have occurred.
  
  It forms a continuous domain with its extension, until the age \( {U} -1 \).              
  From that age on, they form a multi-domain.
  This could only change if the originating colony goes through a next work
  period and kills itself; however, there is not enough time for this:
  the definitions~\eqref{eq:destr-time}, \eqref{eq:compute-start} show that
  \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{destr-t}}}}{Q} \) is much smaller than \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{compute-start}}}} \).

title: Proof
body_md:
et us take times \( v_{2}, v_{1} \) close from below \( \sigma_{2},\sigma_{1} \)
as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:legality} (Legality).
From time \( v_{1} \) on, follow the development of colony \( \mathcal{C} \).
The computation process can be treated similarly to the proof in 
that lemma; but in the communication with neighbor colonies, we must show that all retrieved
information can be attributed to a single time.
By event~\eqref{eq:no-big-damage}, the whole space-time area in
which this communication takes place contains at most one damage rectangle.
Repeated application of Lemma~\ref{lem:creation} (Creation) guarantees the success of
extending arms via the rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Extend\/}}}} \), defined in Section~\ref{sec:growth},
over possible latent or germ cells or an opposing extension arm,
showing that in each direction, within a good time bound either the extension arm of the
colony \( \mathcal{C} \)
reaches its neighbor \( \mathcal{C}' \) (provided it exists) or the neighbor's  reaches it.
If there are extension arms from both colony \( \mathcal{C} \) and a non-adjacent
neighbor colony \( \mathcal{C}' \) then the strength ordering gives preference to one
side and therefore soon only (at most) one arm remains on each side.

\begin{sloppypar}
  In what follows, we call the space-time points \emph{free} if they are outside
  the wake of the damage rectangle (see~\eqref{eq:wake}).
Cell \( x \) is called free at time \( t \) and time \( t \) is called free at cell \( x \)  if \( (x,t) \) is free.
We must find a time during
the communication period \( (0,\ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{compute-start}}}}] \) of \( \mathcal{C} \) introduced in
Definition~\ref{def:expansion-period} to which the retrieval from both neighbors
can be attributed.
Let \( a_{1} \) be the last free time when some cell of \( \mathcal{C} \)
has age \( 0 \), and \( b_{1} \) the first free time when some such cell
has age \( \ensuremath{\mathinner{\textsf{\upshape{compute-start}}}} \), and let \(  J_{1}=(a_{1},b_{1}] \).
By~\eqref{eq:safe-part} and the argument after it, we have 
\begin{align*}
 |J_{1}|>1.5KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}},
\end{align*}
while the unsafe parts of the work period (the dwell period of the big cell simulated by \( \mathcal{C} \))
have a total length \( < 1.5RP^{*}{Q}T^{\bullet} \).
Retrieval by rule \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Retrieve\/}}}} \) in Algorithm~\ref{alg:Retrieve-2} happens
in points of \( J_{1} \) (provided it did not happen earlier) if
a safe \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}} \)  as defined in~\eqref{eq:Safe} has been seen in both neighbors.
We will find a sufficiently large subinterval of \( J_{1}\) when this condition holds.
Let \( m_{1} \) be the midpoint of \( J_{1} \).
\end{sloppypar}

\begin{step+}{retr.middle-live}
  Suppose that at time \( m_{1} \) the big cell \( x \) encoded by colony \( \mathcal{C} \) has a left neighbor big cell,
  encoded by a colony \( \mathcal{C}' \).
  Then there is a time interval \( J_{2}\subseteq J_{1} \)
  of size \(  \ge 0.7KR{Q}{T_{\bullet}} \) in which the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}_{-1} \) read by \( \mathcal{C} \) in \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Retrieve\/}}}} \)
  is safe. 
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
  It follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:present-attrib} that \( m_{1} \) is contained in a dwell period \( D \)
  of the big cell encoded by \( \mathcal{C}' \), of length \( \geT_{\bullet}^{*} \).
  By~\eqref{eq:safe-part}, \( D \) has a subinterval \( J' \)
  of size at least \(  1.5KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}} \) in which the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}_{-1} \) read by \( \mathcal{C} \) is safe.
  Without loss of generality assume that \( J' \) is above \( m_{1} \).
  In the worst case all the unsafe parts of \( D \) may come above \( m_{1} \): still,
  the  part \( J_{2} \) of \( J' \) falling into \( J_{1} \) has a length of at least
  \begin{align*}
   |J_{1}|/2-1.5RP^{*}{Q}T^{\bullet} \ge 0.7KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}}
  \end{align*}
  if \( K \) is large enough.  
\end{pproof}

\begin{step+}{retr.middle-dead}
  Suppose that at time \( m_{1} \) the big cell \( x \) encoded by colony \( \mathcal{C} \) has no left neighbor big cell.
  Then there is a time interval \( J_{2}\subseteq J_{1} \)  of size
  \(  \ge 0.4KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}} \) in which the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}_{-1} \) read by \( \mathcal{C} \) is safe. 
\end{step+}
\begin{pproof}
  Let \( J' \) be the largest subinterval of \( J_{1}\) containing \( m_{1} \) in which \( \mathcal{C} \) has no left neighbor.
  Then either \( |J'|>|J_{1}|/3 \) or there is a subinterval of \( J_{1} \) of size \( \ge |J_{1}|/3 \) that
  either contains a whole work period of a left neighbor of \( \mathcal{C} \) or is covered by it.
  In each case, similarly to the reasoning in part~\ref{retr.middle-live} above,
  a safe time subinterval \( J_{2} \) is found of size at least 
  \begin{align*}
   |J_{1}|/3-1.5RP^{*}{Q}T^{\bullet} \ge 0.4KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}}
  \end{align*}
  if \( K  \) is large enough.
\end{pproof}

We found a time interval \( J_{2} \) of size \( 0.4KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}} \)
in which both \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}} \) and \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}_{-1} \) are safe.
Repeating the argument we find a time interval \( J_{3}\subset J_{2} \)
of size \( 0.1KRP^{*}{Q}{T_{\bullet}} \) in which also \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Age\/}}}}_{1} \) is safe.
  This shows that the \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\texttt{\slshape{Retrieve\/}}}} \) rule will succeed at some time \( t' \)
  during the work period of \( \mathcal{C} \) and the simulation result can be attributed to this time point \( t' \) just
  as Condition~\ref{cond:comput}\ref{i:comput.trans} requires.

title: Proof
body_md:
his proof assumes that in case of conflict, growth to the right is preferred, but this choice 
is clearly arbitrary.    
As in Condition~\ref{cond:comput}\ref{i:comput.creation},
we assume that there is no non-vacant \( \eta^{*}(y,t) \) with
\( 0<|y-x|<{Q} {B}  \), \( t\in[a,a+3T^{\bullet *}] \),
and that for every \( t \) in \( [a,a+3T^{\bullet *}] \) at least one of
\( \eta^{*}(x-{Q} {B} ,t) \) and \( \eta^{*}(x+{Q} {B} ,t) \) is a potential
creator of \( x \).
\begin{step+}{growth.to-right}
  Suppose  \(   x-{Q} {B} \) is a potential creator in \( \eta^{*} \) at some time
  \( t\in[a,T^{\bullet *}] \).
\end{step+}  
\begin{prooof}
  Tracing backward and forward the evolution of the colony of big cell \( x-{Q}{B} \),
  we find a work period \( (t_{1},t_{2}] \) containing \( t \).
  If the computation does not kill the big cell \( x-{Q}{B} \) then it will create
  the big cell \( x \).
  Indeed, the only seeming obstacle to the growth to the right could be some
  non-germ cell \( z \) in its way.
  But Lemma~\ref{lem:present-attrib} (Present Attribution) shows that such a
  \( z \) must be a
  left extension cell of a live big cell \( y \) in \( \left[x+{Q} {B} ,x+2{Q} {B} \right) \), and is
  therefore not stronger than the right growth it is preventing.

  Suppose that the computation kills the big cell \( x-{Q}{B} \).
  Then \( x-{Q}{B} \) could not become again a potential creator for time of length
  \( \ge{p}_{0}{T_{\bullet}}^{*} \).
  By our assumption then by the time \( t_{2}<t+T^{\bullet}<2T^{\bullet} \), the big cell \( x+{Q}{B} \)
  must be a potential creator.
  As above, we would find that it has a whole work period \( (t'_{1},t'_{2}] \)
  containing \( t_{2} \), and its computation cannot kill it because then
  neither \( x-{Q}{B} \) nor \( x+{Q}{B} \) would be a potential creator at time
  \( t'_{2} \).
  So \( x+{Q}{B} \) would attempt to create \( x \): let us show that it will succeed
 before time \( a+3T^{\bullet} \).
  As above, an obstacle to this could only be a non-germ cell \( z \) that is
  the right growth cell of a big cell \( y \) whose body overlaps that of
  \( x-{Q}{B} \).
  But this big cell \( y \) must be new and thus not become a creator for
  a time of length \( \ge{p}_{0}{T_{\bullet}}^{*} \).
\end{prooof}

\begin{step+}{growth.to-left}
  Suppose  \(   x-{Q} {B} \) is not a potential creator in \( \eta^{*} \) at any time
  \( [a,T^{\bullet *}] \).
\end{step+}  
\begin{prooof}
  Then \(   x+{Q} {B} \) is a potential creator in \( \eta^{*} \) at time \( a \).
  As above, we find a work period \( (t_{1},t_{2}] \) of the colony
  \( \mathcal{C}(x+{Q}{B}) \) containing \( a \).
  The computation does not kill the big cell \( x-{Q}{B} \) because then
  at time \( t_{2} \) neither \( x-{Q}{B} \) nor \( x+{Q}{B} \) would be a
  potential creator.
  So \( x+{Q}{B} \) will extend a growth arm to the left, which can only be stopped by some
  non-germ cell \( z \) in the way.
  As in the above reasoning, \( z \) must be a
  right growth cell of a live big cell \( y \) in \( (x-2{Q} {B} ,x] \).
  Because right growth is preferred, this would succeed, creating a cell \( y \).
  If \( y=x \) then \( x \) has become non-vacant, so we are done.

  Let us show that other cases are not possible.
  We cannot have \( y=x-{Q}{B} \) because we assumed that
  \(   x-{Q} {B} \) is not a potential creator during this time.
  The body of \( y \) cannot overlap that of \( x \) (without being equal to it)
  because this was excluded by the original assumption.
  In the remaining case, \( y \) creates big cell \( y+{Q}{B} \) which overlaps
  the body of \( x \) while not equal to it, but this is again just what
  has been excluded.
  \end{prooof}

label: def:color-controlling
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:color-controlling}\index{color control}
  Suppose we are given a medium \( M \), along with a history \( \eta \).
  A set \( E \) of space is \emph{color-fitted} in \( \eta \) at time \( t \)
  if  \( \ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Color\/}}}}(x,t)\le\ensuremath{\mathord{\textsf{\slshape{Color\/}}}}(y,t) \) for every pair of
  cells \( x<y \) whose body intersects \( E \).
  A space-time set is color-fitted if it is color-fitted at each time \( t \).
  Let 
\begin{align}\label{eq:J_t}
 J_{t}=(t-({p}_{0}+2)T^{\bullet},t] .
\end{align}
The set \( E \) is \emph{controlled} in \( \eta \) at time \( t \) if every subinterval \( K \) of
it of size \( {B} \), is within distance \( <2{B} \) of the body of a cell at that time,
and the rectangle \( K\times J_{t} \) intersects the (space-time) body of a cell.
It is \emph{color-controlled} if in addition, the set \( E\times J_{t} \) is color-fitted.
It has color \( c \) if it is color-controlled, and each cell whose space-time
body intersects the set \( E\times J_{t} \) has color \( c \).
